title: Decorator

act2.summary: a new modifier, plus a required ordering constraint between two of them

solutions.title: One Fare interface, one small decorator class per modifier
solutions.tradeoff: A new modifier is one new class, composed by adding one line to calculateFare - the same one line the no-pattern route also needed. The price: each modifier's math is isolated and independently testable, but nothing in any decorator's type says it must wrap before or after another - the order that matters lives only in calculateFare's own sequence of ifs, exactly as fragile as the no-pattern function it replaced.

reviewFocus: Is calculateFare's ordering of the four `if`s the ONLY thing in the entire solution route that encodes the senior-before-student requirement?
If a second call site composed StudentDiscount(SeniorDiscount(fare)) instead of the order calculateFare uses, would anything - the compiler, a runtime check, a test outside act2 - catch it?
Is the walkthrough honest that Decorator did not make this requirement any easier than the no-pattern function did?
Would an ordered pipeline of named stages (see docs/DESIGN patterns discussion) have made the required order an explicit, checkable property instead of an implicit one?
